PullRequest.Title: Add setting-names skill: maturity in tags, not setting IDs
PullRequest.Body:
Agents and contributors regularly add settings like `foo.experimental.bar`. Once the feature graduates, the ID is wrong: it either stays misleading forever or has to be renamed, which needs a migration and still breaks docs, dotfiles, and tooling that reference the old ID.

This adds a `setting-names` skill under `.github/skills` that states the convention:

- Name a setting for what it controls. Express maturity with `tags: ['experimental']` or `tags: ['preview']`, which the Settings editor already turns into a badge, sorting, and `@tag:` filters. `preview` settings must already have their final ID.
- `experimental` is unrelated to A/B experiment control (`experiment: { mode }`), which the existing `experiments` skill covers.
- If a rename can't be avoided, register a migration through `IConfigurationMigrationRegistry` that doesn't overwrite a value already set under the new ID (example included).

Scenarios.Scenario: A contributor or coding agent consults the setting-names skill while adding, renaming, or reviewing a setting ID.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Reading the guidance must finish only when a contributor or agent elects to consult this skill; it is not on any VS Code product startup, rendering, input, or settings critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the added 51-line Markdown skill document.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fixed-size file read when this specific skill is consulted; no per-setting or collection fan-out is defined by the patch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This skill file did not exist, so there was no read of it; there was also no setting-names skill workflow to trigger such a read.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The read gates only consumption of this contributor guidance and is off the shipped product's critical paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One optional skill consultation against one fixed-size 51-line document; no realistic collection increases the operation count in the changed code.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most the host's ordinary single skill-document read for this scenario; the patch adds no fan-out, queue, limiter, sequencer, or burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The skill file is static; loading may be served by the host's normal file/content cache, but the diff defines no cache key, invalidation, coalescing, or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that no shipped-product performance mechanism exists; the only plausible boundary is an optional, fixed-size contributor-tool file read.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Agent-host discovery and caching behavior are not defined in this repository patch, but the resource itself is fixed at 51 lines and cannot create meaningful product performance scaling.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the optional fixed-size documentation read is not a meaningful performance cost and no product runtime path changes.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete one-file patch and its only plausible contributor-tool loading scenario. The Markdown-only change adds no shipped runtime work, scaling boundary, retention, or synchronous UI cost, so no performance finding is warranted.
